newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy CPI seen below 2.0 pct in April - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Italy CPI seen below 2.0 pct in April - JP Morgan.

text.p: Italian annual CPI inflation in April will fall to around 1.9 percent and remain at or below this level until June, a report by JP Morgan in Milan said.
March inflation is seen at 0.1 percent month-on-month and 2.2 percent year-on-year, according to analysts' estimates after preliminary data from 11 sample Italian cities on Friday.
February consumer prices stood at 0.1 percent month-on-month and 2.4 percent year-on-year.
Final March CPI will be released by national statistics institute Istat on April 7.

JP Morgan noted that on a seasonally-adjusted basis, consumer prices rose only 1.2 percent at an annual rate over three months ago, compared with an average pace of 1.9 percent in the previous three months.
It also noted that on a seasonally-adjusted basis, industrial production started the first quarter 0.9 percent below the fourth quarter 1996 average.

JP Morgan said the inflation outlook together with high real interest rates and the stagnant economy creates room for a 75 basis point cut in the Bank of Italy's official discount rate in the second quarter.
The central bank last cut rates by 75 bps to 6.75 percent in January.
Althought the economic case for monetary easing remains strong, prospects for further rate cuts hinge on progress in fiscal policy, the report said.
But the Bank "will probably wait for the approval of the mini-budget - as well as for markets' assessment of its effectiveness - before cutting," the report said.
